AbbVie has ridden a powerful run, with the share price moving sharply higher in recent years, so the obvious question is whether the cash the business can produce really supports a valuation at this level. title: Is AbbVie (ABBV) Undervalued Following Its Oncology Push? - Simply Wall St
content:
AbbVie (ABBV) has moved to widen its cancer footprint through a collaboration with Germany’s Disco Pharmaceuticals on AND gated bispecific therapies for solid tumors, adding external oncology technology to its largely immunology-driven portfolio. Recent price action has been mixed for AbbVie, with the share price up 7.68% over the past 90 days and 24.81% year to date. At the same time, the 1 year total shareholder return of 28.43% and 5 year total shareholder return of 192.43% point to momentum that has been building over a longer horizon as investors react to its oncology deals and immunology pipeline moves. Scan how AbbVie’s oncology shift compares with other potential opportunities by reviewing the hand picked list in the 35 healthcare AI stocks that are also leaning into advanced therapies and data driven medicine. Bulls see AbbVie using oncology deals to reinforce an already profitable immunology engine. Bears worry the price already reflects that optimism. The valuation work now shows which side current numbers lean toward. The narrative fair value of AbbVie at $310 sits above the last close at $286.20, which frames the oncology push inside a wider story about cash generation and concentration risk. According to IamPotato, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the narrative, the key question is how long the current immunology engine can carry the rest of the portfolio. AbbVie has largely completed one of the most closely watched product transitions in pharmaceuticals. Skyrizi and Rinvoq have more than offset the steep decline in Humira, driving double-digit revenue growth and allowing the company to raise full-year guidance. The near-term picture is strong, but the portfolio is now heavily concentrated on these two immunology assets, and longer-term patent and competitive risks remain. That lens matters for the new oncology collaboration. AbbVie generated $66.0b in annual revenue and $10.3b in net income, yet the narrative points out that a very large share of that engine now leans on Skyrzi and Rinvoq, with oncology deals like Disco Pharmaceuticals and Elahere aiming to widen the base rather than replace it. Valuation work behind the narrative uses a 7.75% discount rate and arrives at a fair value of $310, which implies AbbVie is about 8% undervalued relative to the last close. The same framework labels the stock as undervalued against that estimate, even as the official value score is just 2 out of 6 and the 1 year total shareholder return of 28.43% and 5 year total shareholder return of 192.43% already reflect strong past gains. On the cash flow side, the separate SWS DCF model currently values AbbVie at $422.51 per share, which is about 32.3% above the last close of $286.20. That model projects future free cash flows from the existing portfolio and pipeline, then discounts them back using a required return to translate longer term expectations into a single figure today. Those two valuation anchors, the $310 fair value in the community narrative and the $422.51 output from the SWS DCF model, both sit above the market price but rely on different assumptions about how long Skyrizi and Rinvoq can support earnings, how oncology and neuroscience evolve, and how debt, negative equity and dividend coverage are managed over time. Still, the AbbVie story can change quickly if Skyrizi or Rinvoq face sharper competition than expected or if oncology additions fail to offset pressure elsewhere. Find out about the key risks to this AbbVie narrative. There is a catch. While the SWS DCF model points to AbbVie trading 32.3% below its future cash flow value, the market is paying a P/E of 49.1x, above the 47.6x fair ratio, the 45.8x peer average and the 16x biotech industry.
